summary: Earned constraints: a policy enforced only inside its own script is advisory, because any tool with file access routes around it, so the same table is enforced at the editor boundary too; a policy gate fails open on its own defects and closed only on policy, since a guard that can break a session gets disabled and then nothing is enforced; work is claimed before it starts and heartbeated after each write, because a checkpoint written at the end of a cycle is worth nothing to a machine that stops mid-cycle; and an unreleased claim is retained as abandoned rather than cleared, since the fact that a run did not finish is itself the evidence a resumer needs. Observed from A:/ProjectName: hooks there enforce gates but nothing checkpoints, which is exactly the gap the operator hit. Two adoptions from that project remain unbuilt: the governed output contract and the agent directory.
